key_insight: A unified analytical model links loss diagnosis and design guidance for PEC cells by quantifying how light absorption, transport, recombination, and interfacial mismatch limit performance.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers convert experimental current-voltage data into actionable optimization targets for improving photoelectrodes and selecting materials for solar fuel devices.
method: Builds a physically consistent model for both built-in junction and semiconductor-electrolyte junction photoelectrodes.
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency maps, and Sankey-style energy-flow visualizations.
Fits experimental data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms.
evidence_signal: The model is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, and used to compare absorber classes such as Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: Because the framework relies on fitting measured current-voltage data and idealized assumptions, its diagnostic accuracy may depend on data quality and how well real device physics match the model.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
